setup.scope: This market covers olive oil as a finished edible commodity — virgin, extra virgin, and processed/refined olive oil — valued at the point of first sale or consumption, whether sold in bulk or packaged for retail, foodservice, or industrial food use. It excludes non-olive edible oils (palm, sunflower, rapeseed, coconut, mustard), olive-derived non-oil products (table olives, olive pomace, olive leaf extract), and olive oil used as an input to separately valued markets such as cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and personal-care formulations, which are not priced as part of this market. Downstream end-use demand — including foodservice frying volumes, retail packaged-oil sales, and industrial food-manufacturing usage — is used only as an intermediate signal to derive how much olive oil those usages require, and never as a separately valued commodity within this market. Olive oil used in cosmetics or pharmaceuticals is out of scope only where it is not valued as olive oil at all; where such usage is simply an end-use of the same edible-grade oil, it remains in scope.

setup.scope: This market covers olive oil as a finished edible commodity: liquid fat obtained solely from the fruit of Olea europaea (Olea europaea L.) by mechanical or chemical extraction, across all commercial grades (extra virgin, virgin, refined/lampante, and olive-pomace oil) as defined by IOC and Codex Alimentarius standards, valued at the point of production/consumption. It excludes table olives, olive-based cosmetics and soaps, olive leaf extracts, and non-olive vegetable/seed oils, which are separately valued markets. Olive oil used as an input to downstream products (canned fish, sauces, bakery, prepared foods, foodservice) remains in scope, because that usage is a direct demand for olive oil itself; the downstream finished goods are not valued here. Upstream olive growing and olive pomace/residue processing are not separately valued, though olive harvest volumes and crush yields are legitimate intermediate evidence for deriving olive oil output.
